 SECTION A (25 marks)
 Answer all the questions in this section in the spaces provided.
1. A micrometer screw gauge with an error of +0.02 mm shows a reading of 0.31 mm when used
 to measure the diameter of a steel ball. Determine the actual diameter of the steel ball.
 (2 marks)
2. Students want to cut down a tree without destroying any of the houses around it. Describe how
 students can estimate the height of the tree using the height of one student to safely cut down
 the tree. (2 marks)
3. Figure 1 shows a building block placed on a plank of wood supported by two pivots.
 Figure 1
 On the diagram, show how tensional force acts on the plank of wood. (1 mark)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
4. Figure 2 shows a person squeezing a tube of toothpaste.
 Figure 2
 State the principle that is applied in squeezing the toothpaste out of the tube. (1 mark)
5. In a certain experiment, 2 cm3 of dry salt was dissolved in 10 cm3 of water. It was observed
 that the volume of the salt solution was 10.5 cm3. Explain why the volume of the solution was
 not the same as the sum of the individual substances. (2 marks)
6. State one feature of a clinical thermometer that allows the reading to remain constant when the
 thermometer is no longer in contact with the body of a patient. (1 mark)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
7. Figure 3 shows two spanners that can be used to loosen a nut.
 Figure 3
 Explain why spanner B will require less force when loosening the nut. (2 marks)
8. Figure 4 shows an oval ball balanced on the ground.
 Figure 4
 Explain why the ball is said to be in unstable equilibrium. (1 mark)
9. A student is required to calibrate a spring balance for use in measuring weight. Other than the
 spring and the masses, name one other apparatus the student must have in order to calibrate
 the spring. (1 mark)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
10. It is observed that a vehicle travelling on a dusty road leaves a trail of dust rising high above
 the ground. Explain this observation. (2 marks)
11. An object moving with an initial velocity of 3 ms-1 is uniformly decelerated to a stop after
 moving through a distance of 10 m. Determine its acceleration. (3 marks)
12. A student placed a coin on a smooth cardboard which was on top of an empty glass beaker.
 The cardboard was then suddenly pulled horizontally away from the beaker. State and explain
 the observation made. (3 marks)
13. State one source of non-renewable energy. (1 mark)
14. Explain why a person trapped inside a smoke-filled room is advised to crawl along the floor
 towards the exit. (3 marks)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
 SECTION B (55 marks)
 Answer all the questions in this section in the spaces provided.
15. (a) State the meaning of the term specific heat capacity. (1 mark)
 (b) (i) A student observed that when an ice cube is placed in water it melts.
 Explain this observation. (2 marks)
 (ii) State two ways in which the melting point of the ice can be reduced.
 (2 marks)
 (c) A block of ice at 0 ˚C is supplied with 2000 J of heat. Determine the mass of water that
 will melt. (Specific latent heat of fusion for ice is 3.36×105 Jkg-1) (3 marks)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
 (d) A student mixed 25g of hot water at 50 ˚C with 75 g of cold water at 20 ˚C.
 Determine the final temperature of the mixture. (Specific heat capacity of
 water = 42,000 Jkg-1K-1) (3 marks)
16. (a) Students of a certain school want to verify Boyle’s law.
 (i) State two apparatus that the students will need. (2 marks)
 (ii) State one quantity that they would keep constant while verifying Boyle’s law.
 (1 mark)
 (b) Figure 5 shows an apparatus that was used to investigate the rate of diffusion of two
 gases A and B which form a white deposit when they interact.
 Figure 5
 Figure 5
 (i) Identify the gas that diffused faster. (1 mark)
 (ii) State two ways of increasing the rate of diffusion of the two gases in the tube.
 (1 mark)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
 (c)
 (ii) The volume of a fixed mass of gas is 20.0 cm3 at a temperature of 19 ˚C.
 Determine the volume of the same mass of gas when the temperature increases
 to 24 ˚C at constant pressure. (3 marks)
17. (a) Figure 6 shows an object moving at a uniform speed on a circular path of radius r. Given
 that the object moves from point A to B in a time tb seconds:
 Figure 6
 (i) Indicate on the diagram, the:
 (I) angular displacement θ; (1 mark)
 (II) linear displacement S. (1 mark)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
 (ii) (I) write down an expression of the angular velocity ω in terms of t.
 (1 mark)
 (ii) (II) derive an expression for the linear velocity v in terms of the angular
 velocity ω. (2 marks)
 (b) A pendulum bob of mass 20 g is whirled in a circular path of radius 100 cm at a
 velocity of 0.5 ms-1. Determine:
 (i) centripetal acceleration of the bob; (3 marks)
 (ii) centripetal force acting on the bob. (2 marks)
 (c) Explain why a car should reduce its speed when negotiating a sharp corner. (2 marks)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
18. (a)
 (b) To verify Archimedes principle, a student is provided with water in a measuring
 cylinder, a solid metal, a piece of thread and a spring balance.
 Describe how:
 (i) the mass of water displaced may be measured using these apparatus;
 (3 marks)
 (ii) Archimedes principle may be verified. (3 marks)
 (c) (i) State one way of reducing surface tension in liquids. (1 mark)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
 (ii) It is observed that when a certain object is placed in water, it gets fully
 submerged. However, when the same object is placed in glycerine, it is partially
 submerged as shown in Figure 7.
 Figure 7
 Explain this observation. (3 marks)
19. (a) A stone and a piece of paper are released from the same height in a vacuum. It is
 observed that they both hit the ground at the same time. Explain this observation.
 (2 marks)
 (b) A car of mass 1560 kg travelling at a velocity of 25 ms-1 is brought to rest by a
 constant force of 3000 N.
 Determine the:
 (i) change in momentum; (2 marks)
 Certificate of Secondary Education Turn Over
 232/1
 (c) Jane measured the length of the palm of her hand as 18.7 cm.
 (i) Describe how the palm length may be used to estimate the length of a
 laboratory table top. (2 marks)
 (ii) Explain why the estimated length of the laboratory table top in (i) is not
 accurate. (2 marks)
